latin: Ad hoc, ut sit mutuitas realis relationis, requiritur quod fundamentum ex sua natura ordinetur ad aliud, tanquam ad suam perfectionem.
translation: For there to be a real mutuality of relation, it is required that the foundation, by its own nature, be ordered toward another thing, as toward its own perfection.
translation_note: 'Fundamentum': ground of relation. 'Mutuitas realis': real reciprocity.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-swarm-batch5, from Latin at farmer1998:12613

sources.text: Henry of Ghent, Quodlibet III, q. 4; Quodlibet XIV, q. 2
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit traces thesis 12's account of the foundation of a real relation to these two Quodlibetal questions

doctrine: Farmer's note places the thesis within a series on relation that begins at 4.16-17 and continues through 5.11-13 (farmer1998:12655). Edelheit states that 'theses 11, 12 and 13 deal with Henry's notion of relation, a crucial point in Henry's thought which can be found in many different parts of his works' (edelheit2022:15721). He traces thesis 12 to Henry's Quodlibet XIV, q. 2, where Henry holds that real relations require a real diversity in their foundations, so that distinct relations are not similar according to the same measure and thing measured (edelheit2022:15877), and to Quodlibet III, q. 4, where Henry identifies a relation taken 'per se and according to existence' with 'order' (ordo) — the power to found or constitute which thesis 12 attributes to the foundation (edelheit2022:15883).
historiography: Edelheit calls the theses ascribed to Henry among those that 'contain some of the most central philosophical' material in the set, without further specification in the material consulted (edelheit2022:15883, sentence cut off at 'central philosoph-').

quotations.text: Theses 11, 12 and 13 deal with Henry’s notion of relation, a crucial point in Henry’s thought which can be found in many different parts of his works

not_established: The page or paragraph of Henry's Quodlibet XIV, q. 2 and Quodlibet III, q. 4 corresponding to Edelheit's citations is not given in the material consulted.
Whether Pico endorses or merely reports Henry's account of relation beyond stating it is not addressed by the sources consulted.
